# Application map controls

The `application-map` native test uses the public compiler API with exact
original and candidate MLIR bytes. `nested.mlir` exercises declaration-order
roots, repeated and empty protocol applications, an expanded role-free Math
helper, role substitution, a call inside a repeat and a dormant definition.
`zero-ports.mlir` retains distinct logical values of an empty packed product;
physical storage size cannot erase or identify those ports.
`services.mlir` carries two providers with the same contract through one
application without inserting a role restriction on either service operand.

Additional controls use maintained source applications, service repetition and
scoped Func/CF fixtures. Mutations refresh candidate digests before testing
actual SSA operand, return, owner and body changes. The CFG block-order control preserves the
exported logical rows and still requires the independent native comparison to
refuse relocation. JSON controls cover exact shapes, duplicate decoded keys,
identities, canonical ordinals, parents, paths, coverage and work limits.

The supported preparation edge expands protocol applications and pure Math
helpers, retains shared scoped helpers, and inserts exactly the native
port-role restrictions. It works with ordinary `prepareProtocol(..., false)`
outputs within the complete structured-source admission profile. Unchanged
shared pure calls can also remain direct associations. Components are empty
because this edge associates complete logical SSA values. Written links are
null because bytes and diagnostic locations do not supply a checked frontend
association.

Arithmetic folding, common-subexpression elimination, polynomial recipe
realization and selected construction-start insertion are not accepted as
unverified auxiliary rows. The arithmetic-fold control demonstrates this
refusal even when the native preparation API accepts the transformation.
Extending the edge requires the owning specification to publish bounded
independent rules for introduced instructions and eliminated or reused source
results. Extra fields and unsupported rules currently refuse.

The `application-map-cli` test exercises the public commands with exact input
bytes and checks stale-source and incomplete-coverage refusals. C++ cases also
check producer/checker separation and candidate mutations with refreshed digests.
